questions.question: What is Dedoc's core purpose?
options: Convert different document formats into a unified structured representation
Store PDF bytes as database rows
questions.explanation: Dedoc extracts content, annotations, structure, tables, attachments, and metadata into a common output representation.

questions.question: Why should a capacity plan separate native-text and scanned pages?
options: Scanned pages require recognition work that can dominate service time and memory
OCR always makes the output perfect
File count already captures all parser work
questions.explanation: Page rendering, OCR, orientation, and table recognition add substantial work. A single documents-per-hour average hides the workload mix and tail.

questions.question: Which route best fits a PDF containing both native-text pages and scanned inserts?
options: Assume every page has a native text layer
Use automatic PDF routing with page-level textual-layer detection
Flatten the file name into plain text
questions.explanation: Page-level detection allows mixed documents to use native extraction where possible and recognition where necessary.

questions.question: When is disabling PDF table analysis an acceptable optimization?
options: Only when the downstream contract does not require row and cell relationships
questions.explanation: Skipping table analysis can reduce work, but it intentionally gives up structured table output. The consumer contract decides whether that loss is acceptable.

questions.question: Why should parsed output include route and source lineage?
options: To trace quality failures and review important output against the original input and parser configuration
To guarantee no parser bug exists
questions.explanation: Lineage makes parser behavior auditable and supports review, regression analysis, and safe reprocessing after route changes.

questions.question: A worker completes parsing after losing its queue lease. What production property prevents duplicate published results?
options: Idempotent publication under a stable job identity
questions.explanation: Attempts can overlap around lease loss and timeouts. Publishing under a stable job and output version must be idempotent.

questions.question: Which release test is most informative for a parser change?
options: A versioned corpus covering native, scanned, mixed, table-heavy, attachment-heavy, malformed, and adversarial inputs
questions.explanation: Parser changes should be evaluated by document population and structural contract. A broad golden corpus exposes regressions hidden by clean samples and aggregate text counts.
